input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer of fifteen percent of annual Fees for every week an invoice is late. This is not an early-termination fee, is uncapped and open-ended (so it can quickly exceed remaining contract value), and is triggered by a minor breach — walk-away territory and a clear failure of the fallback (which permits only an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount). No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties, or minimum termination charges appear (§ 10 requires only payment for delivered work, and § 27 permits termination without penalty), so the single cure is to remove this charge and confirm the preferred position that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Remove Customer-payable liquidated damages for late payment
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, and a charge of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a late invoice is punitive and could exceed the contract value. We have replaced Section 7.7 with confirmation that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer; if a liquidated amount is unavoidable, our fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole such amount.
